chunks: Say: 'Have you thought of those you invoke apart from God? Show me what they have created of the earth, or, do they have a share in the heavens? Bring me an earlier Book than this, or inherited knowledge, if you are truthful.'
ai.seo_question: What evidence does the Quran demand from polytheists to prove the validity of their idols?
ai.summary: In Surah Ad-Dhariyat, Allah challenges polytheists to prove the creative power of their idols by asking what they have created on earth or what share they have in the heavens. The verse further demands a preceding Book or inherited knowledge to support their claims, concluding with a call for truthfulness. This rhetorical challenge underscores the Shia emphasis on Tawhid by contrasting the limited, created nature of idols with the absolute, uncreated authority of Allah.
